references.text: The Israelites broke camp from Rephidim, mentioned here as the starting point for the journey to the Wilderness of Sinai.
The route from Rephidim is documented in Israel's wanderings through the wilderness.
The Wilderness of Sinai is the place where the Lord spoke to Moses and where the census took place.
God's mountain (Horeb/Sinai) is the place where Moses first met God in the burning bush, and now all Israel comes to this mountain.
God promised Moses that the people would serve him on this mountain after their deliverance from Egypt.
Moses reminds the people that they camped at Horeb (Sinai), the mountain of the Lord.
Stephen refers to Mount Sinai in his speech about Israel's history.
Stephen mentions the assembly in the wilderness at Mount Sinai where Moses received living words.
Paul uses Mount Sinai allegorically when he speaks about the two covenants.
